## Welcome

In this practical part of the course we will work with geospatial data related to a 'hypothetical' conservation project. The tutorials will guide you through the process of collecting field data with QField, analyzing and visualizing it in R, and creating maps in QGIS. With that you sould be able to apply the same workflow to your own field data and conservation projects.

Therfore you will get introductions of - how to use QField for field data collection and biotope mapping, - how to load and analyse your geospatial data in QGis, - how to create maps and use Ellenberg indicator values to assess the habitat status.

In the end you will be able to use the creted maps for your protocols and presentations.

The tutorials are designed to be self-contained, but you can also work through them in any order that suits your interests and needs. The data provided is synthetic example data created for teaching purposes, so feel free to replace it with your own field data when working through the exercises.

## Course structure

| Tutorial | Topic | Software |
|---------------------------|-------------------|---------------------------|
| [QField Tutorial](qfield_tutorial.qmd) | Fieldwork, Biotope types | QField v4.1.12 |
| [QGIS Tutorial](qgis_tutorial.qmd) | Map layers, projections, spatial queries, map export | QGIS 4.0 |
| [R Spatial Tutorial](r_spatial_tutorial.qmd) | Vector/raster analysis, species distribution mapping | R ≥ 4.2 |
| [Cheat Sheet](cheat_sheet.qmd) | Tips and tricks for working with QGIS | QGIS 4.0 |

## Data

Example data used throughout the tutorials live in the `data/` folder:

| File                            | Description                              |
|------------------------|------------------------------------------------|
| `data/Biotope_Mapping.qgz`      | Biotope mapping data (QGIS project)      |
| `data/Biotope_mapping_GroupX.gpkg`      | Biotope mapping data (GeoPackage)|
| `data/Naturschutzgebiete_20XX.gpkg` | Conservation area data (GeoPackage)  |
| `data/Study_areas_20XX.gpkg` | Study area boundaries (GeoPackage) |
| `data/species_observations.csv` | Georeferenced species occurrence records |
| `data/land_cover.tif`           | Land-cover raster (GeoTIFF)              |
| `data/study_area.gpkg`           | Study area boundaries (GeoPackage)             |

> **Note:** The data files provided are synthetic example datasets created for teaching purposes. Replace them with your own field data when working through the exercises. 

## Prerequisites (but not mandatory)

-   Basic familiarity with GIS concepts (coordinate systems, vector vs. raster).
-   R and RStudio (or any R IDE) installed.
-   QGIS 3.28 LTR or newer installed.
-   Quarto 1.4 or newer (only needed to re-render the tutorials).

## Getting started

Clone or download this repository, then open the project folder.\
Render all tutorials at once with:

``` bash
quarto render
```
